text: M&V operating period (1), the HEDS control and optimization system evaluated the ambient and internal conditions and automatically set the control mode to 10 – Cooling With Dehumidifying, which includes dehumidification, while for M&V operating period (2), the HEDS optimization system evaluated the ambient and internal conditions and automatically set the control mode to 8 – Cooling Without Dehumidifying, which does not include dehumidification control. Humidification was necessary during part of the testing period to maintain the RH within the limits required for the museum, but the HEDS does not control the humidifier, which operates independently at the zone level. System mode 8 was also used for the remaining M&V operating periods, (3)-(5). The system modes are automatically selected by the HEDS controller for the operating periods with the HEDS activated, but the weather conditions did not require dehumidification after the initial M&V operating period since dew point return air, ambient air, mixed air and space conditions remained below their respective thresholds to switch back to system mode 10 with dehumidification. For the baseline (non-HEDS) operating periods, system mode 8 was manually set to disable the energy recovery coil and its logic, but the cooling coil (CC) setpoints were maintained at target dewpoint, as is standard practice for CAV and VAV systems that do not include automated controls. Water- and air-side heat balance review: Using a similar validation method as described for the summer data evaluation, we verified that the M&V data gives similar results for the heat transfer calculated using data for the air side and water side flows. The plots in Fig. 7 show very good alignment of the trends between the thermal power metrics for the CAV mode, and the calculated heat transfer data for the air and water side flows differ by less than 10%.
